animal_evidence.endpoint: Macrophage depletion blocks limb regrowth and promotes fibrosis
Hand2-Shh positional memory reprogramming in limb regeneration

human_bridge.interpretation: Translation paths include non-gene interventions; only strict orthology counts identified molecular targets, and none establishes human limb regrowth.

human_context.interpretation: Mammalian regeneration is largely limited to distal digit tips; a review does not demonstrate human whole-limb regrowth.

negative_claims: No human whole-limb regenerative efficacy inferred from orthology.
No successful two-cohort GEO replication inferred from one PASS.
No external review, even positive, substitutes for human biological experiments.
Human digit-tip repair or human fibroblast responses do not establish whole-limb regrowth.
next_falsifiable_test: Institutionally supervised, preregistered human primary-cell study testing macrophage/ECM effects on fibrosis with matched negative controls; evaluate positional signalling separately and never equate an in-vitro response with limb regrowth.
reason: Animal perturbations and human molecular targets cannot establish human limb regeneration; no authenticated, independent human-tissue functional experiment or whole-limb regeneration outcome is present in the evaluated repository evidence.
scientific_question: Can known axolotl limb-regeneration mechanisms work in human tissues?
